questions.name: Introduction to OSHA
questions.objective: 1.1 Explain why OSHA was created and how it supports safe and healthful working conditions
questions.text: Why was OSHA established?

answers.text: To help assure safe and healthful working conditions for workers
To replace every employer safety program with a federal safety manual
To approve every construction schedule before work begins
To guarantee construction work has no remaining hazards

explanations.a: OSHA’s core purpose is to help assure safe and healthful working conditions through standards, enforcement, training, outreach, education, and assistance. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Employers still need effective site-specific safety programs.
explanations.c: OSHA focuses on workplace safety and health, not project schedule approval.
explanations.d: Hazards still exist, so training emphasizes recognition, avoidance, control, and prevention.

questions.name: Introduction to OSHA
questions.objective: 1.1 Explain why OSHA was created and how it supports safe and healthful working conditions
questions.text: What should OSHA 30-Hour Construction training emphasize?

answers.text: Learning how to avoid reporting injuries
Hazard identification, avoidance, control, and prevention
Replacing all task-specific training required by OSHA standards
Memorizing every paragraph number in OSHA standards

explanations.a: Accurate reporting and hazard correction support worker protection.
explanations.b: Outreach construction training is intended to emphasize recognizing, avoiding, controlling, and preventing workplace hazards. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Outreach training does not replace separate training required by specific OSHA standards.
explanations.d: The course is hazard-focused rather than a standards memorization course.

questions.name: Introduction to OSHA
questions.objective: 1.1 Explain why OSHA was created and how it supports safe and healthful working conditions
questions.text: During an OSHA 30-Hour Construction class, a supervisor asks about OSHA purpose and coverage. Which statement best describes OSHA’s role in construction safety?

answers.text: OSHA purchases protective equipment for each employer
OSHA performs daily supervision for every construction crew
OSHA establishes and enforces safety and health requirements and provides assistance and education
OSHA issues building permits for construction projects

explanations.a: Compliance concept: employers are responsible for required protection and safe working conditions.
explanations.b: Prevention focus: daily supervision remains an employer responsibility.
explanations.c: OSHA uses standards, enforcement, outreach, education, and assistance to support safe and healthful workplaces. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Building permits are not OSHA’s main workplace safety role.

questions.name: Introduction to OSHA
questions.objective: 1.1 Explain why OSHA was created and how it supports safe and healthful working conditions
questions.text: Which construction worker is most likely covered by OSHA protections?

answers.text: A self-employed worker with no employees
A family member doing personal work at home
A public employee in every state under federal OSHA rules
An employee working for a private construction contractor

explanations.a: Self-employed individuals without employees are generally not covered in the same way as employer-employee relationships.
explanations.b: Personal non-employment work is outside normal OSHA workplace coverage.
explanations.c: Public-sector coverage depends on state plan arrangements.
explanations.d: OSHA generally covers private-sector workers and employers, including construction employers, unless a specific exception or state plan structure applies. This is the correct answer.

explanations.c: Hazards still exist, so training emphasizes recognition, avoidance, control, and prevention.
explanations.d: Employers still need effective site-specific safety programs.

questions.name: Introduction to OSHA
questions.objective: 1.2 Identify worker rights under OSHA
questions.text: A construction crew is reviewing OSHA responsibilities. A worker wants information about chemical hazards used on the jobsite. Which right applies?

answers.text: The right to receive information and training about workplace hazards
The right to waive all hazard communication requirements
The right to mix chemicals without labels
The right to take any chemical home for review

explanations.a: Workers have rights to hazard information and training they can understand. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Hazard communication requirements are not waived by individual preference.
explanations.c: Labels and hazard communication help workers understand chemical hazards.
explanations.d: Inspection concept: removing chemicals from the workplace is not a worker right.

questions.name: Introduction to OSHA
questions.objective: 1.2 Identify worker rights under OSHA
questions.text: A worker asks for access to exposure records related to workplace health hazards. What should the employer do?

answers.text: Deny access because health hazards are handled only by management
Provide access to applicable exposure records as required
Allow access only after the worker withdraws a complaint
Replace exposure records with verbal reassurance

explanations.a: Worker access to certain exposure information is part of OSHA protection.
explanations.b: Workers have rights to access certain exposure and medical records relevant to workplace health hazards. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Access rights cannot be conditioned on giving up protected activity.
explanations.d: Answer boundary: verbal reassurance is not a substitute for required access to applicable records.

questions.name: Introduction to OSHA
questions.objective: 1.2 Identify worker rights under OSHA
questions.text: Which is a worker right under OSHA?

answers.text: The right to ignore site safety rules that feel inconvenient
The right to approve all employer business decisions
The right to a safe and healthful workplace
The right to remove guardrails whenever work is delayed

explanations.a: Workers must follow safety rules and use required protections.
explanations.b: Worker rights focus on safety and health protections.
explanations.c: Workers have the right to working conditions that do not pose a risk of serious harm. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Removing protective controls can expose workers to hazards.

questions.name: Introduction to OSHA
questions.objective: 1.2 Identify worker rights under OSHA
questions.text: A worker believes a trench lacks protective systems and could collapse. Which OSHA right is most relevant?

answers.text: The right to remove other workers from payroll
The right to redesign the project without employer approval
The right to keep working silently to avoid delay
The right to raise a safety concern or file a complaint

explanations.a: Payroll decisions are not the OSHA right at issue.
explanations.b: Workers can report hazards, but redesigning work is not the same as an OSHA complaint right.
explanations.c: Inspection concept: staying silent can leave a serious hazard uncorrected.
explanations.d: Workers can raise hazards and may file OSHA complaints when they believe unsafe or unhealthful conditions exist. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Introduction to OSHA
questions.objective: 1.2 Identify worker rights under OSHA
questions.text: On site, during an OSHA 30-Hour Construction class, a supervisor asks about worker rights. Which worker action is protected when done in good faith?

answers.text: Reporting a workplace safety hazard
Damaging equipment to make a safety point
Bypassing lockout or guarding because the task is urgent
Falsifying inspection notes to pressure a supervisor

explanations.a: OSHA protects workers from retaliation for exercising safety and health rights, including reporting hazards. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Protected activity does not include damaging property.
explanations.c: Answer boundary: unsafe conduct is not protected simply because work is urgent.
explanations.d: False documentation is not protected safety activity.

questions.name: Introduction to OSHA
questions.objective: 1.3 Identify employer responsibilities under OSHA
questions.text: On site, a construction crew is reviewing OSHA responsibilities. A jobsite has a known fall hazard at an unprotected edge. What should the employer do?

answers.text: Allow work to continue if the crew is experienced
Warn workers verbally while leaving the edge unprotected
Provide and enforce appropriate fall protection before workers are exposed
Wait for an OSHA inspection before installing protection

explanations.a: Answer boundary: experience does not remove the need for fall protection.
explanations.b: Warnings alone may not adequately control a serious fall hazard.
explanations.c: Employers must address recognized hazards such as falls through effective protections and safe work practices. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Hazards should be controlled before an inspection or injury occurs.

questions.name: Introduction to OSHA
questions.objective: 1.3 Identify employer responsibilities under OSHA
questions.text: Which action best supports safe and healthful construction work?

answers.text: Ignore subcontractor hazards that affect other workers
Use production pressure as a reason to bypass protective systems
Rely on luck when tasks are short
Inspect the jobsite for hazards and correct unsafe conditions

explanations.a: Hazards affecting workers on the site need coordination and control.
explanations.b: Compliance concept: production pressure does not justify exposing workers to serious hazards.
explanations.c: Prevention focus: short-duration tasks can still create serious hazards.
explanations.d: Employers should identify and correct jobsite hazards rather than waiting for injuries or enforcement. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Introduction to OSHA
questions.objective: 1.3 Identify employer responsibilities under OSHA
questions.text: What is a basic employer responsibility under OSHA?

answers.text: Provide a workplace free from recognized serious hazards
Correct hazards only after an injury occurs
Shift every safety responsibility to workers by posting a sign
Wait for OSHA to identify every hazard before taking action

explanations.a: Employers must provide working conditions that are free from recognized hazards likely to cause death or serious physical harm. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Hazards should be prevented and controlled before injuries happen.
explanations.c: Employers cannot transfer their core duty by posting a sign.
explanations.d: Employers must identify and address hazards proactively.

questions.name: Introduction to OSHA
questions.objective: 1.3 Identify employer responsibilities under OSHA
questions.text: What should an employer do when PPE is required for a construction task?

answers.text: Tell workers to buy any PPE they personally prefer
Provide required PPE and ensure workers are trained to use it properly
Use PPE as a substitute for correcting every hazard at the source
Allow workers to decide whether eye protection is necessary around flying particles

explanations.a: Required PPE must be appropriate for the hazard and provided as required.
explanations.b: Employers are responsible for required protective equipment and for training workers on proper use when PPE is needed. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: PPE is important, but higher-level controls should be used when feasible.
explanations.d: PPE decisions should be based on hazards.

questions.name: Introduction to OSHA
questions.objective: 1.3 Identify employer responsibilities under OSHA
questions.text: During training, during an OSHA 30-Hour Construction class, a supervisor asks about employer responsibilities. Which employer action supports OSHA training responsibilities?

answers.text: Train only after a worker has already been injured
Use training records to discourage workers from reporting hazards
Train workers in a language and vocabulary they can understand
Give workers a manual in a language they cannot read and mark training complete

explanations.a: Compliance concept: training should occur before exposure to hazards where required.
explanations.b: Prevention focus: training records should support safety, not retaliation.
explanations.c: Training must be understandable so workers can recognize hazards and follow safe procedures. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Training is ineffective if workers cannot understand it.

questions.name: Introduction to OSHA
questions.objective: 1.4 Explain how workers can file complaints and use OSHA resources
questions.text: During training, a construction crew is reviewing OSHA responsibilities. A worker believes a serious hazard exists and the employer has not corrected it. What can the worker do?

answers.text: File a complaint with OSHA
Wait until another worker is injured before reporting
Sign away the right to contact OSHA
Remove all warning signs so OSHA notices faster

explanations.a: Workers may file OSHA complaints about unsafe or unhealthful workplace conditions. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Hazards should be reported before injuries occur.
explanations.c: Workers cannot be forced to give up protected OSHA rights.
explanations.d: Inspection concept: creating additional hazards is not an appropriate complaint method.

questions.name: Introduction to OSHA
questions.objective: 1.4 Explain how workers can file complaints and use OSHA resources
questions.text: Which information helps OSHA evaluate a complaint?

answers.text: A request that OSHA ignore current hazards
A clear description of the hazard, location, affected workers, and employer information
A rumor with no workplace or hazard details
The worker’s opinion about payroll taxes

explanations.a: Complaints are intended to address hazards.
explanations.b: Specific information helps OSHA understand the alleged hazard and determine an appropriate response. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Vague information makes it harder to evaluate and address hazards.
explanations.d: Answer boundary: OSHA complaints should focus on workplace safety and health hazards.

questions.name: Introduction to OSHA
questions.objective: 1.4 Explain how workers can file complaints and use OSHA resources
questions.text: Where can workers find OSHA safety and health information?

answers.text: A private vendor’s advertising page as the sole source
After an OSHA citation has been issued and not before
OSHA publications, the OSHA website, OSHA offices, and training resources
By asking a coworker who has never received training

explanations.a: Private vendors may offer training, but official OSHA resources are also available.
explanations.b: Workers and employers can use OSHA resources before enforcement occurs.
explanations.c: OSHA provides information through publications, online resources, offices, and training and outreach materials. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Official resources provide more reliable guidance.

questions.name: Introduction to OSHA
questions.objective: 1.4 Explain how workers can file complaints and use OSHA resources
questions.text: A worker fears being identified after filing an OSHA complaint. Which statement is most appropriate?

answers.text: The worker loses OSHA protections by requesting confidentiality
The employer chooses whether OSHA keeps the worker’s name confidential
The worker must publicly sign every complaint at the jobsite
The worker can ask OSHA to keep their name confidential

explanations.a: Requesting confidentiality does not remove protected rights.
explanations.b: Confidentiality is requested through OSHA, not decided by the employer.
explanations.c: Inspection concept: workers can request confidentiality when filing a complaint.
explanations.d: Workers filing complaints can request confidentiality so their identity is not disclosed to the employer. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Introduction to OSHA
questions.objective: 1.5 Recognize inspection, citation, recordkeeping, and anti-retaliation concepts
questions.text: Which employer action is prohibited after a worker reports a safety hazard?

answers.text: Training workers on how to avoid the hazard
Documenting the hazard and corrective action
Retaliating against the worker for reporting the hazard
Correcting the reported hazard

explanations.a: Training supports prevention and does not violate worker rights.
explanations.b: Inspection concept: documentation can support accountability and hazard correction.
explanations.c: Workers are protected from retaliation for exercising OSHA rights such as reporting hazards or filing complaints. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Correcting hazards is the appropriate safety response.

questions.name: Introduction to OSHA
questions.objective: 1.5 Recognize inspection, citation, recordkeeping, and anti-retaliation concepts
questions.text: Which statement about inspections citations recordkeeping and anti-retaliation is most accurate? Which situation may involve OSHA recordkeeping requirements?

answers.text: Deleting injury records after a complaint is filed
Recording every personal tool a worker owns
Recording only injuries that the employer chooses to discuss
Recording certain work-related injuries and illnesses on required OSHA forms

explanations.a: Required records must be maintained and not destroyed to avoid scrutiny.
explanations.b: Answer boundary: personal tool inventory is not the injury and illness recordkeeping focus.
explanations.c: Recordkeeping is based on OSHA criteria, not employer preference.
explanations.d: Many employers must keep records of certain work-related injuries and illnesses using OSHA recordkeeping forms. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Introduction to OSHA
questions.objective: 1.5 Recognize inspection, citation, recordkeeping, and anti-retaliation concepts
questions.text: What is the purpose of an OSHA inspection?

answers.text: To determine whether workplace safety and health requirements are being followed
To guarantee the employer will never receive a citation
To replace the employer’s daily hazard inspections
To approve payroll and project billing records

explanations.a: OSHA inspections evaluate workplace conditions, hazards, and compliance with safety and health requirements. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Inspections may result in citations when violations are found.
explanations.c: Compliance concept: OSHA inspections do not remove the employer’s ongoing responsibility.
explanations.d: Prevention focus: OSHA inspections focus on safety and health.

questions.name: Introduction to OSHA
questions.objective: 1.5 Recognize inspection, citation, recordkeeping, and anti-retaliation concepts
questions.text: What can happen when OSHA finds a violation during an inspection?

answers.text: Workers lose their right to report hazards
OSHA may issue citations and propose penalties
The employer no longer has to correct the hazard
OSHA automatically closes the business permanently

explanations.a: Inspection concept: workers retain OSHA rights regardless of citations.
explanations.b: Citations and penalties are enforcement tools used when OSHA identifies violations. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Citations generally require correction of cited hazards.
explanations.d: Enforcement outcomes depend on the violation and process.
